key_insight: Clean pages have an authoritative copy elsewhere, so detect-and-refetch can replace correction; Linux already drops poisoned clean page-cache pages and rereads them.
killer_doubt: At 1% BER a 64-byte line is clean with probability 0.99^512 = 0.6%, so nearly every access refetches from SSD (~50-100 us). Works only below ~1e-7 BER.
decisive_experiment: DRAM-Bender characterization of ~100 reject or downbinned DDR4/DDR5 dies: are failures clustered (map-out-able rows/columns) or diffuse, and what share of wafer starts they are; plus a refetch-latency model. ~$80k.
prior_art: Heterogeneous-Reliability Memory (Luo et al., DSN 2014: parity plus recovery of clean pages from storage); Linux hwpoison clean-page handling; downbinned DRAM resale.

key_insight: Geometric draw-down sets 10-50 nm layer thickness with no lithography; thickness control in drawn laminates is genuinely free and kilometre-scale.
killer_doubt: A 1000-10,000x draw breaks molten Sn-Zn layers (viscosity ~1e-3 Pa s) by Plateau-Rayleigh breakup; crystalline oxide semiconductors cannot co-draw with glass; ribbon tiling needs ~10 nm contact registration.
decisive_experiment: Draw a glass/oxide/metal laminate preform 1000x on a university draw tower (Clemson, UCF, MIT); TEM layer continuity at 20-50 nm and test any transistor action across the ribbon. ~$150k.
prior_art: MIT Fink lab multimaterial fibers (in-fiber diodes, digital fibers with embedded chips); Bilkent iterative-draw nanowires; UCF in-fiber capillary breakup. No drawn memory cell.

key_insight: Draw-redraw gives billions of AR~100 coaxes with no etch: a 5 um slice with 20 nm core and 5 nm k~7 glass holds ~5 fF per coax.
killer_doubt: Cell-level bonding at DRAM pitch (~40-50 nm) is ~10x finer than today's ~0.4-1 um hybrid-bond pitch, draw disorder defeats registration, and molten metal cores bead up below ~100 nm.
decisive_experiment: Draw-redraw an etchable-core glass bundle to 50-100 nm pores, slice 5 um, ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN, then measure fF/um2, leakage and pore-position disorder versus an ideal lattice. ~$250k.
prior_art: NRL nanochannel glass (Tonucci et al., Science 1992, ~33 nm channels by draw-redraw); microchannel plates; Phase B N-21 anodic-alumina capacitor template, which is cheaper.

key_insight: Helium's small kinetic diameter makes membrane enrichment easy where it is concentrated (leak check, tool returns), turning a geopolitical exposure into an on-site loop.
killer_doubt: Backside helium leaks into chambers and leaves in ~10-50 slm dry-pump N2 ballast at roughly 100-1,000 ppm with fluorocarbon/HF; 70-90% fab-wide recovery from that stream is implausible.
decisive_experiment: With a fab partner, log helium concentration and flow per exhaust source for one week by mass spectrometer, then cost recovery per Mcf at the measured dilution. ~$100k.
prior_art: Industrial-gas helium recovery units (membrane plus PSA) already serve optical-fibre draw, MRI and research labs; the service model is offered by gas majors.

key_insight: Same core mechanism as I-10762 (H2 backside gas instead of helium); adds a Pd-membrane return of used H2 to the forming-gas header.
killer_doubt: Returning chamber-exposed H2 to gate forming-gas anneals risks F/Cl contamination to save a gas costing ~$2-5/kg; the recycle adds risk without value. Merged into I-10762.
decisive_experiment: Covered by the I-10762 experiment; add an RGA impurity check of backside-return H2 only if recycling is still wanted. ~$20k increment.
prior_art: None found for H2 backside gas (one search): chuck patents list He, N2 or Ar (via search snippet). Pd purifiers are commercial.

key_insight: Free-molecular gap conductance scales as (g+1)/(g-1)/sqrt(m): H2 gives ~2x helium per unit accommodation, and its Paschen minimum (~270 V vs ~155 V) lowers backside-arc risk.
killer_doubt: Unverified share of fab helium that is backside cooling (A2 flags it), and plasma impact of ~0.5-2 sccm H2 leaking into fluorocarbon HAR etch; H2 LFL is 4%.
decisive_experiment: University ICP etcher with thermocouple wafers: wafer temperature with He versus H2 at 5-15 Torr under 1-3 kW bias, plus HAR etch rate, selectivity and profile with 0-2 sccm H2 bleed. ~$250k.
prior_art: None found (one search): ESC patents name He, N2 or Ar backside gas (via search snippet). H2 is already a W CVD and epi gas.

key_insight: Inline cache-line compression behind CXL multiplies logical capacity for compressible cold data with no new device, only a controller.
killer_doubt: Already productized: server data compresses ~1.5-2x on average, and vendors ship or specify it. A $1M FPGA card adds nothing an incumbent lacks.
decisive_experiment: No novelty experiment needed. If pursued, a trace-driven compressibility study of production AI and database heaps on an existing CXL compression expander. ~$50k.
prior_art: IBM MXT inline main-memory compression (2001); Marvell Structera A CXL expander with inline LZ4 (2024); ZeroPoint Technologies compression IP.

key_insight: A flood ion beam self-organizes 20-40 nm gratings in one cheap step; phase-locking to a coarse pre-pattern mirrors graphoepitaxy for block copolymers.
killer_doubt: Ripple order lengths of ~0.1-1 um imply ~1e8 dislocations/cm2 versus near-zero for DRAM lines; SAQP on ArF already makes array gratings without EUV, so the saving is small.
decisive_experiment: Broad-beam Ar+ on a-Si over 200 nm-period guide trenches; SEM defect counts over 1 mm2 versus guide period and fluence, against a block-copolymer DSA baseline. ~$80k.
prior_art: Bradley-Harper theory (1988); HZDR and IOM Leipzig ripple studies; directed self-assembly (IBM, imec, Merck) is the stronger self-patterning route and still unadopted.

key_insight: An activation already restores a row; data whose proven lifetime is under worst-case retention never needs refresh, and a hardware deadline fault makes this safe.
killer_doubt: AI data lives too long: KV caches persist seconds to minutes and training activations ~0.1-10 s per step, against the 10-50 ms window; short-lived data already sits in SRAM.
decisive_experiment: Trace allocation-to-last-read lifetimes in LLM serving and training HBM, and measure the share of bytes and refresh energy under 32 ms; DRAM-Bender tail retention at 85 C. ~$100k.
prior_art: RANA (ISCA 2018) refresh-optimized eDRAM using data lifetime in DNN accelerators; Smart Refresh (2007); RAIDR (2012); Phase B N-64 lifetime-leased refresh.

key_insight: On-panel oxide decoders and muxes make panel memory addressable without millions of bonded lines; display gate-on-array and IGZO microprocessors show n-only oxide logic already ships.
killer_doubt: p-type SnO/Cu2O reach only ~1-5 cm2/Vs with poor on/off, and oxide-TFT Vt sigma of ~30-100 mV rivals a ~100 mV bitline signal, forcing offset-cancelled sense amps.
decisive_experiment: On a university or foundry oxide-TFT line, build n-only auto-zeroed sense amps reading 2T0C gain-cell columns; measure offset, sense time versus bitline C, and energy at 85 C. ~$300k.
prior_art: Display gate-on-array oxide drivers; PragmatIC Flex-RV IGZO RISC-V (Nature 2024); SnO/Cu2O CMOS inverters (NOVA Lisbon, KAUST); SEL CAAC-IGZO logic.

key_insight: Winding is the cheapest way to stack area volumetrically; roll-to-roll at ~$2-10/m2 would be striking if TFT memory arrays survived on web.
killer_doubt: Schoopage end-spray is a blanket contact that shorts every turn's edge together, so separate per-turn buses are impossible; web distortion of ~100-1,000 ppm (0.1-1 mm/m) defeats micron overlay.
decisive_experiment: Paper and CAD first: per-turn edge interconnect count and a schoopage-compatible bus scheme. Then a single-imprint (SAIL-style) TFT array on polyimide at 1-2 um, measuring yield per m2. ~$200k.
prior_art: HP Labs self-aligned imprint lithography (SAIL) for roll-to-roll TFT backplanes; metallized-film capacitor winding; flexible oxide TFT-on-foil (Holst Centre, PragmatIC).

key_insight: Display fabs process ~170x more area per month than a DRAM fab at under half the capex; transistor-written oxide gain cells need no HAR capacitor, EUV, W, Hf or He.
killer_doubt: Economics need F<=0.3 um with ~8F2 cells over 20 tiers. Gen-10.5 FPD steppers resolve ~1.2-1.5 um, giving ~37 GB/m2 and ~$13/GB, worse than DDR5's $1.48/GB cost.
decisive_experiment: On Gen-2/3.5 glass at a display R&D line: two-tier ZTO 2T0C arrays by step-and-repeat NIL at F=0.3-0.5 um; measure tier overlay after 350 C cycles, Vt sigma and 85 C retention. ~$700k.
prior_art: Phase B N-38 panel-level oxide memory; SEL DOSRAM/NOSRAM CAAC-IGZO memory on silicon; no DRAM on display panel lines found (one search).
